rci9_site_effect_handling.detail: The reference cohort for the normative model was the HCP dataset, which, although a consortium, used a single customized scanner for T1-weighted image acquisition. Therefore, there were no multi-site effects to be harmonized within the training data itself. The paper addresses potential site confounds in the application phase by only comparing patients and controls from the same respective datasets (NUSDAST, ABIDE), not by applying a harmonization method to the reference data.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Group comparisons of the overall deviation metric between patients and controls were conducted using a two-tailed Mann-Whitney U test. Regional differences in reconstruction error between groups were also assessed using the Mann-Whitney U test, with Cliff's delta to measure effect size.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: A deep autoencoder trained on a large healthy cohort successfully identified distinct patterns of neuroanatomical deviation in individuals with schizophrenia and autism spectrum disorder, yielding significant group differences in deviation metrics and highlighting disease-specific regional alterations.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: The deep autoencoder produced significantly higher deviation metrics in patients with schizophrenia (p = .001) and autism (p < .001) compared to their respective controls. The normative model's classification performance was comparable to an SVM, achieving an AUC-ROC of 0.707 for schizophrenia and 0.639 for autism. Regional analysis identified distinct patterns of neuroanatomical deviation for each disorder. For schizophrenia, the most significant deviations were in the left ventral diencephalon, left and right lateral ventricles, and right superior temporal cortex. For autism, significant deviations were found in the left choroid plexus, right cuneus, and left putamen, broadly consistent with findings from the existing literature.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: The study notes several limitations: 1) High individual variability in deviation metrics may limit single-subject discrimination. 2) The model was not validated against potential confounding effects of head motion. 3) The fully automated preprocessing pipeline without visual QC could be a source of artifacts. 4) The non-linear nature of the model prevents determining the direction (increase/decrease) of the detected regional alterations. 5) The use of regional features (ROI) results in low dimensionality and potential loss of information compared to voxel-based approaches.
caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: This observation may restrict the possible use of this metric to discriminate patients with a neuropsychiatric disease from healthy people at the individual level. ... Another limitation of our investigation is that subtle differences in head motion may have influenced the estimation of the deviation metrics. ... Another possible source of artifacts in our investigation relates to the preprocessing of the images. ... Finally, due to the nonlinear nature of the model, our method does not allow one to establish the direction of the alterations (i.e., increase vs. decrease in volume/thickness)...

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: The study utilized a semi-supervised learning approach within the deep autoencoder to explicitly model and 'disentangle' the effects of age and sex. The model's performance was directly compared to a traditional machine learning classifier (SVM) using AUC-ROC. The analysis strategy intentionally avoided direct comparison between the two different clinical disorders by restricting statistical tests to within-dataset comparisons (e.g., SCZ vs. controls from NUSDAST) to avoid site-related confounds.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: This study is a notable example of using a deep learning method (deep autoencoder) for normative modeling, as opposed to more traditional statistical methods like GAMLSS or Bayesian regression. A key methodological feature is the semi-supervised framework used to control for age and sex by integrating their prediction into the model's loss function. The study also provides a direct comparison of the normative model's ability to classify patients against a standard SVM classifier.
